claims.summary: On an n>=4 graph of edge expansion epsilon>0 with nonzero total F3 charge, any refutation of vertex equations by scalar multiplication and binary linear combination has a line with vertex potential support in[n/3,2n/3) and at least epsilon*n/6 nonzero edge coefficients. The final potential is a nonzero constant; the first large support is the union of two smaller ones, and a nonzero level-set cut gives expansion. For fixed-degree constant-expansion families, exact fixed-depth AC0[2] circuits for all such line predicates on the whole valid one-hot cube must include a superpolynomial-size line, by fixing one active edge and reducing to MOD3 on Omega(n) bits. This is a restricted charge-derivation representation lower bound; extraction from arbitrary Frege is unproved.
claims.assessment: Working all-parameter balanced-support proof and circuit restriction, medium reviewed. DAG reuse and cancellations are allowed. No claim that general Frege lines are charge equations, no new circuit lower bound, and no PC-degree conclusion. Compatible with the older balanced character-cut upper proof.
